title: GraphCast: Skillful Medium-Range Weather Forecasting
hook: A graph neural network predicts 10-day global weather in under a minute on one machine, matching or beating physics-based forecast models on most variables.
key_points: Encodes Earth's atmosphere as a multi-mesh graph; message-passing propagates information across scales.
Trained on 39 years of ERA5 reanalysis data, predicting the next 6-hour state autoregressively.
Generates a 10-day, 37-level global forecast in roughly 60 seconds on a single TPU.
Outperformed ECMWF's HRES (a leading physics model) on the majority of tracked variables.
content_html: Lam and colleagues at Google DeepMind introduced GraphCast, a graph neural network for medium-range weather forecasting. Originally posted to arXiv in December 2022, an expanded version was published in Science in 2023. The model matches or beats ECMWF's high-resolution physics-based forecast on many standard metrics.
extra_html:
How it works

GraphCast represents the atmosphere as a hierarchical multi-mesh graph - a set of nodes covering the globe at multiple resolutions - and uses three learned GNNs to encode atmospheric state, perform message-passing over the graph, and decode back to a latitude-longitude grid. Given the current and previous 6-hour atmospheric state, it predicts the next 6-hour state; rolling this out autoregressively produces a full 10-day forecast.

Why it matters

Traditional numerical weather prediction solves partial differential equations on supercomputers over hours. GraphCast runs on a single accelerator in under a minute, opening up the possibility of ensemble forecasting at far lower cost and enabling faster iteration on forecast systems. It also suggests that decades of reanalysis data are enough to teach a data-driven model the effective dynamics of the atmosphere. See the arXiv paper for the full benchmark comparisons.

flashcards.prompt: How does GraphCast represent the atmosphere and produce a forecast?
flashcards.back_html: As a hierarchical multi-mesh graph; learned GNNs encode the state, do message-passing, and decode. It predicts the next 6-hour state and rolls out autoregressively to 10 days.

flashcards.prompt: What is GraphCast's key practical advantage over traditional numerical weather prediction?

choices.text: It produces a 10-day forecast in under a minute on a single accelerator
It requires no training data at all
It needs no atmospheric observations as input

flashcards.explanation_html: Traditional NWP solves PDEs on supercomputers over hours; GraphCast runs in ~60 seconds on one TPU, enabling cheap ensembles.

flashcards.prompt: How did GraphCast compare to ECMWF's HRES physics model?

choices.text: It matched or beat HRES on the majority of tracked variables
It lagged HRES but ran faster
It only matched HRES for short 1-day forecasts

flashcards.explanation_html: GraphCast outperformed ECMWF's leading physics-based HRES forecast on most standard metrics.
